packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-19 - unverified image reading (first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of the fragment text. The binding's paper title label (visible in image-001) reads "Selecta / Historia Stamsens. / a / S. R. Sch." with a pencil shelfmark "Stams, StA, Fig. 221(?)h" - that is the host volume, not the fragment, and I did not use it to identify anything.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview, outer face of binding opened flat)
- image-001 shows the outside of a paper-covered binding (marbled paper, vellum spine strip, paper title label on the front board at right). Left half = back board, right half = front board.
- Parchment corner pieces cut from a liturgical(?) manuscript are pasted at the four corners (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). Each shows a few lines of a large gothic textualis in black ink, with red ink (rubrics / red initials) visible: a red initial at top-right corner, and red initial(s)/red text at bottom-left and bottom-right.
- The corners are folded/turned so text runs at various angles (diagonal / upside down). Each corner shows only fragments of perhaps 6-10 lines; lines are cut at both ends by the corner shape. Single column visible per piece; no ruling width or margins can be judged.
- Observation only: large, widely spaced textualis with red initials suggests a liturgical book, but that is tentative.

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-002 (native tile: top-left corner piece of image-001, i.e. back board, top outer corner)
Text is upright but tilted ~25 deg (lines descend to the right). Deskewed crop: crop-02.jpg.
Script: large gothic textualis, black ink; a tiny red speck to the left of line 3 (possible remnant of red ink / rubric). Lines cut at left and right by the corner shape; left edge of block is the turn-in, right edge lost under marbled paper. Line numbers counted from top of the visible text block.
Two groups: lines 1-3 (upper right, shorter) and lines 4-6 (lower left); there may be a lost line between 3 and 4 (spacing is larger), uncertain.

image-002 l.1   ...]lita(?) [first letter before l unclear: a? i?]
image-002 l.2   ...]ca prim(?) / pristi(?) [last letters cut; "pri" clear, then m or sti]
image-002 l.3   ...]men   [probably "amen"/"-men"; first letter lost; red speck at left of the line]
image-002 l.4   ...] m[illegible, abbreviated, stroke above]m(?) [illegible] et meri[...  [ "et meri" fairly clear; last letter possibly cut (meri(t-)?) ]
image-002 l.5   absolu[illegible 1-2]ie(?) et ego   ["absolu" fairly clear, then smudged; "et ego" clear]
image-002 l.6   ..]ū nūn(?) [or "dn̄i"? abbreviation stroke over 2nd word] pape uici(s)? [last word "uic.." ending smudged: uicis / uicāṙ?]
Limitations: heavy staining and smudging; only short fragments of each line; no full words between lines 4-6 left edges.

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-003 (native tile: top-right corner piece of image-001, i.e. front board, top outer corner)
Text upright, tilted ~38 deg (lines rise to the right). Deskewed crop: crop-03.jpg.
Single column; left ends of lines appear to be the true line beginnings (text block starts at an aligned left margin, with red initials hanging into it); right ends cut by the corner/turn-in. Two red initials: one 2-line initial at l.4 (looks like a V), one 2-line initial at l.10 (D or O-shaped, possibly with penwork). Black ink, textualis. Punctus used mid-line (l.7, l.8).
Line numbers counted from top of the text block.

image-003 l.1   et vite ete[...]   [after "vite": "ete" then cut; possibly "eter-", not completed]
image-003 l.2   tuarū [d?]ona(?)[...]   [2nd word: d/t + "na"; uncertain]
image-003 l.3   solū in corpor[...]   ["in corpor" - "corpor" partly stained, fairly clear]
image-003 l.4   [V red initial] irtutū celesti[...]   (Virtutum)
image-003 l.5   omnē languo[r?...]   [indented under initial]
image-003 l.6   cepti tui potestate
image-003 l.7   famule tue. ut fi[...]
image-003 l.8   receptis. u[...]ne(?) [word after punctus faint: "uirtute"? "uīnē"? - leave uncertain]
image-003 l.9   nitate bn̄d[...]  (b(e)n(e)d-?)  [abbreviation stroke over "bn"]
image-003 l.10  [red initial, D? O?] (D?)e s(?)[...]   [black "e" after the initial; next letter cut]
image-003 l.11  [illegible, one letter "h"?] - lost at the turn
Limitations: right ends of every line lost; l.8 and l.10-11 partly lost.

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-004 (overview): the same outer face as image-001, photographed rotated 180 deg (title label now upside down at lower left). Its top corners = the bottom corners of image-001. Top-left of image-004 = bottom-right of image-001 (front board, bottom corner); top-right of image-004 = bottom-left of image-001 (back board bottom corner, with red initial and red rubric text). No new text beyond the four corner pieces. In this orientation the two corners at top of image-004 show their text roughly upright.

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-005 (native tile: top-right corner of image-004 = bottom-left corner of image-001, back board)
Text tilted ~36 deg (lines rise to the right). Deskewed + autocontrast crop: crop-05.jpg.
Left ends of lines are true line beginnings (aligned left margin; large red initial hangs in it); right ends lost at the turn and under damage/abrasion. Upper half heavily abraded (white losses).
Features: a RED RUBRIC LINE IN GERMAN (l.8), followed by a large red decorated initial (c. 3 lines high, l.9-11, with pen flourish to the left). Black text in Latin before and after.
Line numbers from top of the text block.

image-005 l.1   C̄omissa(?) q[...]   [first word "(C/O)missa" with stroke over the first letter; then q + lost]
image-005 l.2   orantib(us) c(?)[...]   ["orantib9", 9-shaped -us sign; next letter c/e, stained]
image-005 l.3   q(ui)b(u)s(?) te rem[...] / ret[...]   [first word "qbs" or "quibs"; "te" clear; "rem/ret" then lost]
image-005 l.4   delic[te?] et [illegible]   ["delic" clear; next letter e/t; "et" (or tironian et) then illegible stained word]
image-005 l.5   nore litterarū(?) [illegible] [...]   ["nore" with stroke over e? (-nore / honore?) ; "littera" clear, ending with stroke]
image-005 l.6   l(?)nū pe(r)mane[...]   ["pe" + "man" fairly clear; first word 3 minims + u with stroke - uncertain]
image-005 l.7   sione inuoc[...]   [then stained, illegible]
image-005 l.8   (RED) Das ist aber ain a[...]   [German rubric; "Das ist aber ain" clear; next word begins "a"/"d", rest lost]
image-005 l.9   [large red initial, B? R? double-bowled form] [illegible 1-2 letters] catur(?) [illegible]
image-005 l.10  [initial cont.] [illegible] ue(?) the(?)[...]   [heavily abraded]
image-005 l.11  [initial cont.] soluat nu[...]   [first black letters after initial: "soluat"; could be the end of a word whose first letter is the initial - not asserted]
image-005 l.12  [t?]p(er)?tate(?) h[...]   [reads "tprtate"/"trītate"; uncertain]
image-005 l.13  uetifi[...]   [or "letifi-"; first letter u/l with stroke over]
image-005 l.14  nb[...] (from image-005 uncropped, bottom; 2 letters only)
Limitations: right half of each line lost; abrasion over l.1-4 and l.9-10. Initial letter identity uncertain.

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-006 (native tile: bottom-right corner of image-001 = top-left corner of image-004, front board)
Text upright, tilted ~24 deg (lines descend to the right). Deskewed + autocontrast crop: crop-06.jpg.
Left edge of the piece cuts across the line starts (first letters lost on several lines); right ends lost at the board edge. Red: a red initial E at the start of l.5 (hanging in the left margin), and a small red letter/mark at the right end of l.4 (after "amen.") - possibly the start of a red rubric continuing beyond the cut. Faint pink/red trace at right of l.6.
Line numbers from top of the visible text block.

image-006 l.1   [...]u[...]   (only a letter or two)
image-006 l.2   [...]ritorū nec m[...] / n[...]   ["ritorū" clear (-ritorum); "nec" clear]
image-006 l.3   [...]lic̄(?) m(at)ris(?) ecclesie [...]   [first word "lic/lit" + stroke (cut at left); "mr̄is" with abbreviation = matris; "ecclesie/ecclētie" - the s may be a long-s/t]
image-006 l.4   [...]i(?) et sp(irit)s s(an)c(t)i. amen. [small red letter]   [written "sp̄s sc̄i"; "amen." clear]
image-006 l.5   (red E)go remitto tibi pen[...]   ["Ego remitto tibi" clear; "pen" then cut]
image-006 l.6   [...]e illi puritati [illegible 1 word: "Kr."?] fa[...]
image-006 l.7   [...]uand(o?) babtizatus fuisti [...]   [first word cut at left: q?/i? + "uand" + o/w; "babtizatus" - spelled with b-b as written, fairly clear; "fuisti" clear]
image-006 l.8   [...]ecclesie se ꝯtendunt(?) & h[...]   [the sign before "tendunt" looks like con- (ꝯ) or p- with stroke (pre-); after "tendunt" a flourish/mark then "&" and "h"]
image-006 l.9   [...](a/e)ccesseris remaneat tib[i...]   ["ccesseris remaneat" clear; first letter a or e]
Below l.9: blank stained parchment (lower margin? or simply lost) - cannot tell.
Limitations: line starts and ends cut; l.6-8 middle partly abraded.

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-007 (overview): INSIDE of the binding (pastedowns, paper, blank, watermark visible; pencil shelfmark "Stams, StA, Frg. 221v(?)" at lower right). The parchment corner pieces' turn-ins show on the inside: top-left (larger turn-in, several lines, upside down/rotated in this view), top-right (narrow strip, 2-3 lines), bottom-right (small, 2-3 short lines), bottom-left (tiny trace, no readable text in the overview). These turn-ins are the continuations/other side of the corner pieces seen outside; which outer corner each belongs to follows from position (inside top-left lies behind the outer front-board top corner when the volume is opened - not asserted beyond position).

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-008 (native tile: inside top-left corner of image-007 - turn-in of a parchment corner piece onto the pastedown)
Two layers of parchment visible: a folded flap (centre, paler, lines tilted ~32 deg rising right) and the turn-in strip along the left board edge (text running roughly vertically, reading bottom-to-top). Pastedown paper overlaps much of it. Small red speck before l.2 of the centre piece. Combined deskewed crop: crop-08.jpg (top = centre flap, bottom = left strip rotated).

Centre flap (lines from top):
image-008 c.1   [...]au(?)[...] / [..]o e[...]   [fragments of 1-2 lines above, cut by fold; illegible beyond single letters]
image-008 c.2   [red speck] [..]t̄(?) / om̄ps cr[...]   [the word "omps" with abbreviation stroke (o/m + p + s) - possibly om(nipoten)s, not asserted; then "cr" + 1-2 letters]
image-008 c.3   [...]io(n?)is ku(?)[...]   ["ioomsku" as seen; uncertain letter division]
image-008 c.4   [...]ns. vt [d/c?][...]   ["ns." then punctus, "vt" clear]
Left strip (reading bottom-to-top along board edge):
image-008 s.1   [...]rit̄ [...]   (rest illegible)
image-008 s.2   [...]ēmus(?) / aqmus(?) [...]   (very uncertain)
image-008 s.3   [...]oue / aue[...]   (very uncertain)
Limitations: very small exposed area, abraded, partly under paper; readings here are low confidence.

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-009 (native tile: inside top-right corner of image-007 - narrow turn-in strip along top edge)
Text upside down in the tile as photographed. Rotated crop: crop-09.jpg (rotation leaves a residual tilt of a few degrees, lines rising right). Part covered by a translucent paper layer (pastedown) through which letters show faintly. A red speck (rubric/red stroke) at left of l.3.

image-009 l.1   [...]uū(?) / unā [...] ꝑ hanc s[...]   ["ꝑ hanc" fairly clear: p with crossed descender = per, then "hanc"; preceding word ends in "-nā"/"-uā" with stroke; next word starts s/f]
image-009 l.2   [...][illegible, under paper]a(?) nec[...]   ["nec" (or "ne" + c) clear at right]
image-009 l.3   [..]r.[red speck] ꝑ ac(?)[...]   ["r" then punctus, red mark, then p with stroke and "ac"/"at"; low confidence]
Limitations: tiny exposed strip; most letters cut by the fold.

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-010 (native tile: inside bottom-right corner of image-007 - small turn-in)
Text tilted ~35 deg; deskewed + enlarged crop: crop-10.jpg. A fold crease runs through the middle; faint red trace at the lower edge (bottom right).

image-010 l.1   [...]ci3 / ei3(?) [...]   (3-shaped final sign, possibly -us/-et; low confidence)
image-010 l.2   [...]tuicaui(?) / uocaui(?) [...]   [first letter tall (t/R?), then "u/n" + "icau/rau" - very uncertain]
image-010 l.3   [...]ctiuu / etiaw(?) [...]   (very uncertain)
Limitations: 3 fragments of words only; low confidence.

================================================================
SUMMARY OF WHAT WAS READ / NOT READ
- Selected spans: all exposed text on the four outer corner pieces (image-002, -003, -005, -006) and the three inner turn-ins (image-008, -009, -010). All tiles in the packet were viewed and read; there was no further text to select.
- Most connected readings: image-003 l.4-9 ("[V]irtutum celesti... / omne languo[r] / cepti tui potestate / famule tue. ut fi... / receptis ... / nitate bn̄d..."), image-006 l.2-9 ("...ritorum nec ... / ... matris ecclesie / ... et sp(iritu)s s(an)c(t)i. amen. / [E]go remitto tibi pen... / ... illi puritati ... / ...quando(?) babtizatus fuisti / ... ecclesie se ꝯtendunt(?) & h... / ...ccesseris remaneat tib[i]"), image-005 incl. a red German rubric "Das ist aber ain a[...]".
- Observations: Latin text in a gothic textualis of medium-large module, single column, with red initials (2-3 lines) and at least one red rubric in German. Content is prayer-like with second-person address ("tibi", "famule tue"); interpretation beyond that is not offered.
- Limitations: each corner piece shows only a triangle of the leaf; line beginnings preserved on image-003 and image-005, line ends lost everywhere. Whether the four pieces come from one leaf or several, and which face of which leaf, cannot be determined from the images. Insides (008-010) are small, abraded, partly under paper; low confidence.
- A wider view would require lifting the pastedowns/corner pieces; no adjacent crop in the packet would add text.
- I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (viewed PROMPT.md and packet images; made rotated/contrast crops in rscratch/packet-19). I did not stop on the image limit.
